scope: Only inactive helper source and CPU safety fixtures; no runtime activation, real signal, process mutation or main evaluation outcomes read.

original_source_review.finding: A helper-local STOP created before cleanup did not prevent SIGTERM. A mocked-only reproduction delivered one mocked SIGTERM.
original_source_review.resolution: Revised cleanup_guard checks local STOP, registration digest and source-bound registration before each signal, including after durable intent I/O. The real-guard counterexample now produces zero signal calls.

passed_boundaries: Only original waves59..63 under original finite deadline; unchanged science plans and no consumed-wave retry.
Complete last RAM-reserve traceback plus unchanged actual progress/log for at least120 monotonic seconds; no performance or scientific outcome trigger.
Exact original driver/owner identities, ancestry/cwd/command and frozen registry/source/job/session/launch/dispatch/plan identities; independent process-group ancestry census.
Shared schedule lock through signal sequence; fresh identity/progress/census after each durable per-signal intent.
SIGTERM first; at least15 seconds before SIGKILL, unless exact leader exits; fresh identity check required for KILL.
Helper-local STOP, original owner STOP/deadline and changed source/registration prevent a subsequent signal.
Exclusive fixed actual01 receipt directory; no helper-created global/startup STOP and no queue-complete or owner-exit fabrication.
limits: No filesystem receipt and signal syscall can be atomic. A durable intent proves intended action only; a missing post-signal receipt cannot prove nondelivery. Final audit must retain any intent/failure and reconcile with native-owner records.

Process-group enumeration and killpg are not kernel-atomic. The source narrows the race with repeated exact identity and ancestry checks while holding the schedule lock; no absolute PID-reuse or uncooperative external mutation guarantee is claimed.

After SIGTERM, log/progress changes or natural identity disappearance cause conservative failure/no KILL. This may leave work for native-owner cleanup and must not be called successful complete cleanup.

A zombie/exited leader does not prove every descendant exited. The helper explicitly leaves reaping to the native owner; final exact helper/worker/descendant census and native-owner closure remain required.
Evidence I/O failure may prevent final receipt writing. Source does not manufacture successful reaping or queue completion; final closure must inspect actual process and owner state.
activation: Not performed or authorized by this review. Any optional activation still requires separate concrete root registration and actual closure review.
